grillFuelTypes.name: Commercial Charcoal Briquettes (Direct Radiant Embers, ~750°C / 1380°F)
grillFuelTypes.fuelClass: Compressed Charcoal & Mineral Ash Binders (Intense Embers, High Smoke)
grillFuelTypes.smokeParticulateDensity: Extreme (Fat drips directly onto 750°C coals, pyrolyzing instantly into dense aerosol plumes)
grillFuelTypes.description: Standard compressed briquettes generate intense localized infrared heat. When rendered animal fat (triglycerides) drips onto embers exceeding 700°C, lipids crack via free-radical pyrosynthesis into Benzo[a]pyrene, Chrysene, and Benz[a]anthracene, carried upward in thick smoke plumes.

grillFuelTypes.name: Natural Hardwood Lump Charcoal (Pure Carbonized Wood, ~850°C / 1560°F)
grillFuelTypes.fuelClass: Pure Pyrolyzed Hardwood (Ultra-High Radiant Infrared, Zero Starch Binders)
grillFuelTypes.smokeParticulateDensity: High to Extreme (Extreme localized radiant heat; high flare-up potential from molten drippings)
grillFuelTypes.description: Burns significantly hotter than briquettes with faster airflow. Extreme temperature accelerates meat surface Maillard amine-creatine condensation, while fat drippings trigger violent localized flare-ups with instantaneous polycyclic hydrocarbon synthesis.

grillFuelTypes.name: Propane Gas Grill with Flavorizer Deflector Bars (~450°C / 840°F)
grillFuelTypes.fuelClass: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (C3H8 Combustion, Vented Deflector Plates)
grillFuelTypes.smokeParticulateDensity: Moderate (Inverted metal flavorizer bars vaporize fat, generating localized flare-ups)
grillFuelTypes.description: Propane burns cleanly to carbon dioxide and water vapor. However, fat dripping onto metal burner guards or flavorizer shields heated to 400°C–500°C still pyrolyzes into aromatic hydrocarbons, though at roughly 60% lower volume than charcoal.

grillFuelTypes.name: Piped Natural Gas Grill (~420°C / 790°F)
grillFuelTypes.fuelClass: Compressed Methane (CH4 Clean Combustion, Low Soot Deflector Bars)
grillFuelTypes.smokeParticulateDensity: Moderate-Low (Clean methane burn; deflector plate contact accounts for >90% of PAHs)
grillFuelTypes.description: Slightly lower BTU output than propane. Produces minimal combustion soot, with PAH formation restricted almost exclusively to grease flare-ups on heated flame tamers beneath the grill grate.

grillFuelTypes.name: Hardwood Pellet Smoker / Convection Grill (Indirect Airflow, ~120°C–180°C)
grillFuelTypes.fuelClass: Compressed Hardwood Sawdust (Thermally Regulated Indirect Convection)
grillFuelTypes.smokeParticulateDensity: Controlled Wood Smoke (Wood lignin phenolic aerosols, but zero direct fat-on-ember pyrolysis)
grillFuelTypes.description: Features a solid metal deflector plate that routes rendered fat away into a grease bucket, preventing direct contact with the fire pot. Lower cooking temperatures keep meat surfaces below the critical 150°C threshold for heterocyclic amine formation.

grillFuelTypes.name: Electric Smokeless Indoor Contact Grill (~220°C / 430°F)
grillFuelTypes.fuelClass: Enclosed Sheathed Nichrome / Ceramic Element (Zero Open Flame)
grillFuelTypes.smokeParticulateDensity: Negligible (Drip tray keeps fats cool; zero hydrocarbon pyrolysis from open combustion)
grillFuelTypes.description: Eliminates open flame combustion and ember flare-ups completely. Rendered fat falls through grates into a water-cooled reservoir, suppressing over 95% of volatile PAHs and generating only mild surface HCAs.

meatProfiles.name: Ground Beef Burger / Ribeye Steak (20% Fat, High Muscle Creatine Pool)
meatProfiles.description: Maximum dual-hazard matrix. High lipid content yields heavy fat dripping onto hot coals, driving intense PAH smoke plumes. Simultaneously, high endogenous creatine and phenylalanine concentrations drive massive PhIP and MeIQx synthesis on charred crusts.

meatProfiles.name: Skin-On Chicken Thighs / Drumsticks (15% Fat, Extreme PhIP Susceptibility)
meatProfiles.description: Highest known food matrix for 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP). High free phenylalanine amino acid pools in poultry muscle combine with skin fat flare-ups to produce peak mutagenic heterocyclic amine yields.

meatProfiles.name: Bone-In Pork Chops / Loin (8% Fat, Moderate Creatine)
meatProfiles.description: Moderate lipid and creatine content. Fat cap trimming dramatically reduces dripping flare-ups, while surface doneness control prevents heavy MeIQx accumulation.

meatProfiles.name: Atlantic Salmon Fillet (12% Omega-3 Fat, Low Creatine Matrix)
meatProfiles.description: Polyunsaturated fish fatty acids drip and smoke readily if placed directly on hot grates, generating moderate PAHs. However, low creatine reserves keep heterocyclic amine formation significantly below terrestrial red meats and poultry.

meatProfiles.name: Plant-Based Pea / Soy Protein Burger (14% Coconut/Canola Oil, Zero Animal Creatine)
meatProfiles.description: Contains vegetable lipids that can drip and smoke, generating minor PAHs on charcoal. However, the complete absence of animal creatine virtually abolishes polar heterocyclic amine (PhIP, MeIQx) synthesis.

cookingDoneness.name: Rare / Medium-Rare (Internal 52°C–57°C / 125°F–135°F, Minimal Bark)
cookingDoneness.description: Meat surface dwell time is brief and surface temperature barely breaches the 150°C threshold required for intensive Maillard amine-creatine cyclization. Crust remains soft and uncarbonized.

cookingDoneness.name: Medium (Internal 60°C–65°C / 140°F–150°F, Golden-Brown Crust)
cookingDoneness.description: Standard grilling doneness. Surface temperature reaches 170°C–180°C, producing distinct Maillard browning and moderate PhIP formation alongside baseline smoke condensation.

cookingDoneness.name: Well-Done (Internal 71°C+ / 160°F+, Dark Crispy Exterior)
cookingDoneness.description: Prolonged exposure dehydrates the surface crust, driving surface temperatures past 200°C. Heterocyclic amine concentrations spike nearly 4-fold over medium, with extensive lipid dripping.

cookingDoneness.name: Heavily Charred / Blackened (Internal 77°C+ / 170°F+, Carbonized Crust)
cookingDoneness.description: Extreme pyrolysis. The exterior crust undergoes complete carbonization, generating massive quantities of mutagens (PhIP, MeIQx, Benzo[a]pyrene) concentrated in the black exterior bark.

marinadeMitigations.name: No Marinade: Dry Salt & Pepper Only (Baseline 1.0x)
marinadeMitigations.mechanism: Zero chemical inhibition. Meat surface amino acids and creatine react unimpeded, while rising smoke particles adhere directly to molten surface fat.
marinadeMitigations.description: Standard baseline grilling. Provides zero antioxidant or physical barrier against thermal amine condensation or smoke aerosol adhesion.

marinadeMitigations.name: Dark Beer / Stout Marinade (Melanoidins & Free-Radical Scavengers, -68% PAH / -55% HCA)
marinadeMitigations.mechanism: Stout beer contains high concentrations of melanoidins and polyphenols that trap reactive oxygen and carbon radical intermediates during lipid pyrolysis and Maillard cyclization.
marinadeMitigations.description: Validated by European Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry: soaking steaks in dark ale for 2 hours reduces Benzo[a]pyrene accumulation by 68% and cuts PhIP formation in half.

marinadeMitigations.name: Fresh Rosemary, Thyme & Garlic Marinade (Carnosic & Rosmarinic Acid, -88% HCA / -40% PAH)
marinadeMitigations.mechanism: Carnosic acid, carnosol, and rosmarinic acid in rosemary act as extraordinarily potent free-radical chain breakers, dismantling the pyridine and imidazole condensation rings.
marinadeMitigations.description: The gold-standard culinary antioxidant: Kansas State University food science trials showed rosemary extract halts up to 88%–90% of all heterocyclic amines without altering cooking doneness.

marinadeMitigations.name: Lemon, Apple Cider Vinegar & Garlic Marinade (Acidic Protonation, -65% HCA / -35% PAH)
marinadeMitigations.mechanism: Low pH (pH 3.0–3.5) protonates amine groups on amino acids, preventing nucleophilic attack on creatinine carbonyl intermediates.
marinadeMitigations.description: Acidic marinades suppress the Maillard reaction pathways that assemble mutagenic ring structures, while garlic allicin provides additional radical-quenching sulfur compounds.

marinadeMitigations.name: High-Sugar BBQ Sauce Applied EARLY (Molasses/Honey Glaze, +180% PAH / +240% HCA Char)
marinadeMitigations.mechanism: Reducing sugars (fructose, glucose) caramelize and burn aggressively at temperatures above 160°C, producing a thick, charred carbon crust that traps rising smoke particles.
marinadeMitigations.description: A critical grilling hazard: brushing sugary barbecue sauce onto meat at the start of cooking causes severe burning and crust carbonization, multiplying carcinogen concentrations over twofold.

grillingGeometry.name: Direct Heat Close to Coals / Flame (5–8 cm / Direct Fat Drips into Fire)
grillingGeometry.description: Direct radiative proximity maximizes flare-ups. Molten lipid droplets splash onto embers only inches below, creating intense upward thermal smoke jets that blast the meat underside.

grillingGeometry.name: Direct Heat on Elevated Grate (15–20 cm above Embers)
grillingGeometry.description: Standard direct grilling geometry. Convective dispersion dissipates a portion of rising smoke particulates before impingement on the meat surface.

grillingGeometry.name: Indirect Two-Zone Setup with Drip Pan (Zero Fat on Heat Source)
grillingGeometry.description: Coals or active gas burners are banked to one side; meat rests on the opposite side over an aluminum water drip pan. Eliminates 92% of fat pyrolysis smoke plumes, virtually eradicating PAHs.

grillingGeometry.name: Protective Perforated Grill Pan / Parchment-Foil Shield
grillingGeometry.description: Physical metal or cedar barrier intercepts direct flare-ups and diverts grease away from embers while permitting steam and gentle convective cooking.

consumerProfiles.name: Standard Adult (70 kg Body Weight, Normal Hepatic CYP1A2 Metabolism)
consumerProfiles.description: Cytochrome P450 1A2 and glutathione S-transferases in the liver biotransform dietary HCAs into Phase II excretable conjugates, but high single-meal doses saturate metabolic clearance.

consumerProfiles.name: Frequent Griller / BBQ Enthusiast (70 kg, High Cumulative Exposure 8x/Month)
consumerProfiles.description: Repeated chronic exposure leads to steady-state DNA adduct accumulation in gastrointestinal epithelial cells and colorectal mucosa, lowering individual tolerable intake buffers.

consumerProfiles.name: Pediatric Child (25 kg Body Weight, Heightened Toxicological Vulnerability)
consumerProfiles.description: Lower body mass and developing hepatic enzyme pathways make children vulnerable to 2.8x higher systemic carcinogen dosage per gram of grilled meat consumed.
